experiments.scope: Checks of O. Goldzweig's published 38-step collision and of the exact counts his attack (ePrint 2026/2913) relies on; proof.md Sections 3, 4, 10.3. One check per trial; a trial returns a pair only if its check passes. Trial 0: the published pair M0||M1, M0||M1' (a full collision of the target) if the chaining value, outputs, padded digest, the core A3..A13 of both executions, the variant, lower part, upper pair, key, every difference of the paper's Table 6 and every Table 2 condition on the pair's words are recomputed from the pair. Trials 1..6: exact counts over 2^32 by carry paths and GF(2) elimination: |V7| = 16,384 in 512 complete aligned blocks of 32 (row 22); 4 values of W8 (row 23); 3,276,800 (row 25, tau = 6002033f); 637,534,208 (row 26); 637,534,208 (row 17); 536,870,912 (row 30). Trial 7: 1,572,864 variants of the core (E6 with dW9 = 0 and solvable dW8 = -4), one E5 pattern each, the published one among them; 16 random variants built end to end follow the pair's differences through step 17. Trial 8: 64 random lower candidates of the published variant with random W1..W6, W7 uniform in V7 and W0 fixed by the key 00b50618: the chaining value is solved from W0..W7 (Section 2 bijection) and both executions follow the pair's differences through step 17. Randomness for trials 7 and 8: SHAKE-256 of a label and the organizer trial seed. Trials 9..255 return no pair by design.
experiments.hypothesis: Returned pairs: 9 (trials 0..8, every check passes); full collisions of the target: 1 (trial 0, the published pair of the paper's Table 5; trials 1..8 return a fixed non-colliding marker pair). What a pass shows: the published pair is a collision of the selected target; the core, variant and key recovered from it are those stated in the paper; the exact counts that set the lower-solution rate (|V7| / 2^32 = 2^-18) and the expansion conditions (rows 17, 23, 25, 26, 30) hold; the state differences through step 13 hold for every chaining value and lower candidate, and steps 14..17 depend on the lower solution only through the key. What it does not show: the rates of the paper's Table 4 (matches, steps 18 and 19, the tail), which need the 5.44 GB table, and any attack cost. Validation by us: two runs in the pinned image, byte-identical output, under 2 seconds; the counts equal a 2^32 brute force in C.

experiments.scope: An independent Python port of steps 1 to 4 of P2 (proof.md Section 5), whose normative statement is the C program of proof.md Appendix A, run on two A14 values against the table that C program built. Trial 0, A14 = 5bde5962 (the published one): a14ok; pairs_for on the first 2^16 points of each affine space of x = E15 (Gray-code order) must give the expected pairs; each of the 192 valid pairs of the C build must pass piok with its class; for the published pair (A15 9b3a6d8a, class 7) kpi must give 2,496 keys including 00b50618, and live() on every one of them must mark exactly the 789 keys the C build stored as live, the published key among them. Trial 1, A14 = 4f9d3ed0: the same walk-prefix and validity checks; kpi on all 256 valid pairs must give 1,024 keys, and live() on every entry must mark exactly the 304 keys stored by the C build, in the same 2 pairs. Expected values: counts from single-A14 runs of the C build and digests of the stored live keys (table/chunk4.bin, chunk0.bin). Each trial returns a non-colliding marker pair only if every comparison holds; trials 2..255 return no pair by design. Deterministic, no randomness beyond the per-entry splitmix64 seeds of P2.
experiments.hypothesis: Returned pairs: 2 (trials 0 and 1), full collisions: 0. What a pass shows: the Python port of P2 and the stored C build agree on every valid pair, key and live verdict tested, including the full key and liveness sets of the published pair and of every pair of A14 = 4f9d3ed0, so the port computes the functions of the normative C program on every case tested. What it does not show: the full walk of x = E15 (about 10 s per A14 in Python; compared in full outside the organizer for both A14 values), the other 262,142 A14 values, and the step-18, step-19 and tail rates. Validation by us: two runs in the pinned image, byte-identical output, 7.4 s under amd64 emulation and 3.5 s natively; changing one expected value makes the trial return no pair.
